subject: Staff briefing: tactical triage, commitments and QBR asks
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com; Gina Park <gina.park@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staff briefing: tactical triage, commitments and QBR asks

All —

Quick readout for today (short bullets + asks). Putting this on the leadership distro for visibility ahead of the QBR packet lock on Friday.

Wins
- Canary completed for v1.3 routing changes: 2% error-rate improvement on p95 inference for sampled queries; latency median stable.
- QBR pack draft (attached) includes updated economics slide and regional latency heatmap.

Risks / Current chokepoints
- Autoscaler behavior on multi-tenant pools is producing short-lived capacity gaps during cold-bursts (we saw 12% increased tail latency at 0800 PT).
- Dependence on the new KV-cache optimization: if we roll without the cache fallback path, we risk a regression in long-tail queries.

Asks (clear, time-boxed)
1) Approve limited canary expansion to 20% traffic (today) to collect end-to-end telemetry (will run 48h). Need laura/lauren approval.
2) Karthik: please provide a cost delta estimate for the 20% expansion (tokens/day baseline + egress) by EOD.
3) Jonas: ops please confirm runbook updates and oncall assignment for the next 48h.

Attachments: QBR_pack_v2.pdf (key slides), canary_runbook.xlsx (runbook + rollback steps).

Notes: I called out the capacity anomaly in slide 7 and a short-run mitigation in the appendix. If we get the green on canary expansion, we can include preliminary numbers in the QBR slide set tonight.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staff briefing: tactical triage, commitments and QBR asks

Lauren —

Thanks for the concise readout. Quick follow-ups:
- I'll surface a cost delta this afternoon. I need the traffic profile for the 20% expansion (per-region split). Can you confirm whether the canary will be routed to multi-tenant or dedicated pools?
- If we hit the cold-burst anomaly again, we need a short-term throttle policy in front of the autoscaler (ops can roll a config to cap burst by region).

Also looping in laura and jonas for runbook and exec-side signoff.

Thanks — read and approve limited expansion to 20% for 48h. Conditions:
- Include a mandatory fallback flag (if KV-cache misses > 8% for 15m, auto rollback to 5%).
- Ops needs to confirm oncall coverage for two windows in the 48h (UTC 07:00–11:00 and UTC 19:00–23:00).

Please update the canary_runbook.xlsx with those two items and post the runbook link to the incident channel before expansion.

Ack — expanding the plan and next steps below.

TL;DR: Canaries go to 20% now (48h). Runbook updated and pushed; fallback flag + oncall windows added. Cost delta in progress from Karthik; I'll add an appendix slide to the QBR pack with the estimated range.

Action items assigned (owner / ETA)
- Lauren: kick the 20% canary expansion (now) and monitor dashboards (ongoing).
- Karthik: cost delta estimate + regional traffic split (EOD).
- Jonas / Ops: confirm oncall and post runbook link to #ops-canary (within 30m).
- Laura: signoff confirmed.

Gina (Acme) — we included a very short note in the QBR appendix intended for your team on expected latency variance during the canary window. If you'd like to pause your non-critical testing to reduce background noise, let me know; otherwise we'll proceed and share telemetry.

Forwarded for context: attached QBR_pack_v2.pdf, canary_runbook.xlsx.

Thanks everyone — I'll share the canary dashboard link in the channel and file a short post-mortem template in case we need one.

Lauren
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
